newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Rains to help Argentine wheat sowing - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Rains to help Argentine wheat sowing - analyst.

text.p: Storms sweeping Argentine grain areas Friday should recharge soils with water in areas hit by drought and prepare them for wheat sowing, but might also slow fieldwork, a grains analyst said Friday.

"This is helping in the areas which have had problems with dryness," Cereal Elevators Association analyst Armando Casalins told Reuters, "But it might cause some delays, and even a switch to shorter cycle wheat in places where soil moisture was already good."
He added that he was still not sure how much water had fallen in southern Santa Fe and the province of Cordoba, the areas which have been most affected by dry weather.

But Casalins said that he still expected wheat area to fall by about 10 percent from the 1996/97 season, when farmers produced a record 16.1 million tonnes of wheat from 7.3 million hectares, according to the government.
The Agriculture Secretariat reported Thursday that farmers had already begun sowing the first long-cycle wheat by June 6.
